ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing Act 2020; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2019; International Companies (Registration and Licensing) Regulations 2017; SIFA Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Rules 2021

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport for each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary public in the UBO's country of residence plus the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT) in case of local notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (POA) executed by each shareholder and director for the Samoan registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the signatory's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit consolidated domestic sanctions and terrorist designations, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and Samoan national police criminal-history databases; enhanced due diligence (EDD) and verified source-of-funds documentation is required for any politically exposed person (PEP) or tax-exempt offshore structure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry (SICR) online e-Registry portal operated by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official company names must be registered in English or Samoan using Latin script. A Chinese or other non-Latin name may be adopted only as a reserved foreign-language alias after clearance, and the corresponding English/Samoan transliteration must be submitted as the primary registered name. All registry filings and certificates are issued in English only.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is refused, the applicant may submit a Notice of Appeal against Name Refusal to the Registrar of International Companies within 14 calendar days from the date of written refusal. The notice must state why the proposed name is not prohibited, misleading, or contrary to public policy. The Registrar must issue a written determination within 21 working days; if the appeal fails, a fresh name reservation may be filed. A name reservation may be extended for an additional fee of USD 25 before expiry; after expiry a new reservation application is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable as the administrative business address for a remote EdTech subscription company, but a physical Samoa street address must be maintained through a licensed registered agent for service of process and statutory notices. A P.O. box alone is not permissible as the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; for a non-licensed, low-risk EdTech/language-learning entity conducting no regulated financial services, SIFA and the registered agent on-site inspection probability is estimated at under 5% per annum, with most supervision performed through documentary review and electronic filings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018), Sections 5 and 12 (Incorporation) and Section 18 (prohibition on domestic trading)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement; subscription may be in any currency and no escrow or deposit obligation is imposed on initial share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers listed in the Memorandum and Articles of Association be and they are hereby approved to subscribe to the initial authorized share capital in the respective amounts set opposite their names; that the registered office address in Samoa designated by the company's registered agent be and is hereby fixed as the company's official registered office, and such registered agent be retained on the terms previously supplied; that [Name] and [Name] be and they are hereby appointed as first director(s) and officers, with authority to open bank accounts, execute agreements, hire professionals, and conduct business; and that all actions taken by the incorporator before this meeting are ratified. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through a licensed SIFA registered agent, specifying a proposed corporate name ending in 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. The Registrar verifies the name against the national register and reserves the approved name for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Letter of instruction to the registered agent
Identity verification of the proposed subscriber or agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is unavailable or conflicts with an existing registration, the agent may submit up to three alternative names on the same application; the re-submission fee is nominal and no duplicate search is charged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Charter Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent licensed under the International Companies Act 1987
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association in conformity with the Act. The subscriber executes the documents and, where the Registry requests notarial attestation, the execution is certified by a notary public authorised in Samoa.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (English)
Consent to act as first director
Consent of registered agent
Subscriber KYC file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises objections to the submitted provisions, the registered agent will redraft the affected clauses and re-submit the M&A for subscriber execution; the 30-day name reservation period remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files Form IC-1, together with the executed M&A, consents, and supporting declarations, with the Registrar. The prescribed government fee and any stamp duties are paid at the cashier window or online portal, and a stamped receipt is obtained.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consents of first director and registered agent
Declaration of compliance with the Act
KYC/AML documentation for all subscribers, directors, and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registered agent files a written response with corrected or supplementary information within ten business days; minor clerical mistakes in the M&A may be cured by filing a memorandum of correction with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Record
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation, the certified Memorandum and Articles of Association, and a certificate of incumbency if requested. The company becomes a separate legal entity on the date stated in the certificate.
required_dossiers: Incorporation application reference number
Official receipt for payment of government fee
Certificate of Incorporation issuance request (if any additional certified copy is required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains typographical errors or an incorrect issue date, the registered agent files an application for rectification together with the original certificate; corrected certificate is issued within three business days without additional filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Establishment of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the International Company, convened by the Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board holds its first meeting (physically or by video conference) and adopts the first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. The company then opens its statutory registers at the registered office in Samoa.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the First Board Meeting
Register of Members
Register of Directors and Officers
Registered Office Address Agreement
Company Seal adoption record (if a seal is used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum is not achieved at the first board meeting, alternative directors or proxies are authorised by the subscriber; the minutes may be ratified at a subsequent board meeting held no later than thirty days thereafter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - International Company is restricted from domestic commercial activity under Section 18 of the International Companies Act 1987 and no physical industrial premises are established
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating licence required for a purely digital EdTech subscription platform; the company is registered as an offshore international company and may conduct global digital commerce without a local business license

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - virtual software operation generates no physical construction, manufacturing, or land disturbance
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable - no wastewater, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), or hazardous waste are generated or discharged; end-user data is stored in cloud infrastructure outside Samoa and is not subject to local effluent or emissions thresholds

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable - the company has no physical workplace in Samoa; records are maintained at the registered agent's office under the International Companies Act 1987, and no fire safety, structural load, or occupational workplace clearance is required for the company's registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue, Samoa (formerly Samoa International Financial Authority; online filing through the Ministry of Revenue Taxpayer Access Portal: https://tap.revenue.gov.ws)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 2016 must apply to the Ministry of Revenue for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and a GST registration number (if required). The application must be filed by a licensed Samoa registered agent using Form IRD-002, including certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, registered office certificate, particulars of directors and shareholders, contact information of beneficial owners, and expected activity declaration. The Ministry will issue a TIN within 10 business days; the IC is also required to obtain a Business License if any physical presence is established, but offshore-only ICs use the registered agent as the official local address for tax correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An International Company is by default a tax-exempt entity under the International Companies Act 2016 and the Income Tax Act 2015. No check-the-box election exists; the exemption is mandatory provided the company derives only offshore income (non-domestic-source income). The IC may elect to be treated as a taxable domestic company by giving written notice to the Ministry of Revenue or by carrying on business within Samoa through a permanent establishment, thereby forgoing the tax exemption. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Samoa has no hybrid mismatch rules, and ICs cannot be treated as partnerships or disregarded entities. An IC can, however, elect in its Articles to become a 'Foreign Company' registered under the Companies Act 2006, but that terminates the IC tax-exempt regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Goods and Services Tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1996, as amended)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 200,000 annual taxable turnover (compulsory registration); voluntary registration permitted with approval from the Ministry of Revenue
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, e-invoicing API, or digital stamping regime at this stage. VAT-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices containing the words 'tax invoice', seller's name and GST registration number, invoice date, description of supply, GST amount, and total consideration. Tax invoices may be issued electronically in PDF or machine-readable format. For exports, the supplier must issue a zero-rated tax invoice and retain evidence of export within 28 days after the supply; all GST filings are submitted via the TAP portal. The Ministry has adopted OECD global digital economy guidance, but no separate digital services tax or real-time transaction clearance applies to online sales by International Companies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1996 when provided to a person outside Samoa, or services that are performed outside Samoa and for direct use or enjoyment outside Samoa. An EdTech language-learning subscription supplied through Apple App Store or Google Play to non-resident consumers qualifies as an export of services, provided the customer's registered address, IP address, and bank/payment card location indicate non-Samoan residence. Digital services that are delivered to end-users in Samoa (including tourists temporarily in Samoa) are standard-rated at 15%. The IC may zero-rate all subscription sales if it contracts with the app store platform operator (Apple/Google) as the customer, treating the platform as a non-resident recipient; evidence must show the platform accepts the digital content offshore. No special digital export license is needed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for physical goods or any bundled tangible components)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (where applicable to physical goods)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit statement showing foreign currency receipt for the exported supply
Non-resident customer declaration or export service contract
IP geolocation and platform sales reports from Apple/Google listing each transaction by country
GST zero-rated schedule reconciling aggregate subscription revenue to platform payout reports
Registered agent's declaration of export substantiation and any e-invoice file for delayed invoicing jurisdictions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry of Revenue may apply a 150% shortfall penalty on any falsely zero-rated supply, plus interest at the prescribed rate from the date of the original refund, and may claw back refunds paid within the prior five years. For intentional evasion, penalties increase to 300%, with fines up to WST 25,000 and imprisonment up to seven years. Directors and the registered agent may be jointly and severally liable for GST clawbacks and penalties if they knowingly assisted in false export documentation. The Ministry may deregister a GST-registered IC and impose a 100% late filing penalty if evidence of export is not maintained for seven years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) — administering the Exchange Control Act 1976 and Exchange Control Regulations 1977 on behalf of the Minister of Finance; the international-company regulatory overlay is administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) pursuant to the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa maintains a managed-float currency (Samoan Tala, WST) that is fully convertible for current-account transactions through authorized dealers, but residents remain subject to CBS exchange-control declarations and prior-approval gates for capital-account movements. A Samoa International Company is statutorily exempt from exchange-control restrictions under section 77 of the International Companies Act 1987, allowing it to hold, borrow, lend, and transact freely in any foreign currency without CBS consent. Dividend and profit remittances from the IC bear no Samoan withholding tax and require no repatriation clearance. Practical friction is therefore confined to resident operating entities and WST-denominated balances; the IC should adopt USD as its functional treasury currency so that Apple IAP/Google Play Billing settlements (USD/EUR) bypass the WST conversion layer entirely.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For Samoan-resident trading companies, export proceeds must generally be repatriated to Samoa and surrendered through an authorized dealer within six months of export unless a CBS exemption is granted; this statutory surrender regime does not apply to a non-resident International Company because section 77 of the International Companies Act 1987 disapplies the Exchange Control Act 1976 to ICs. Accordingly, EdTech subscription revenue collected via app-store rails may remain offshore in USD/EUR wallets and is subject to neither mandatory WST conversion nor forced repatriation. Any service fees subsequently paid by the IC to a Samoan-resident operational parent would enter Samoa as current-account inflows carrying the standard authorized-dealer documentation trail and CBS reporting obligation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Foreign-Currency Operating Account / Capital Escrow Account
USD Foreign-Currency Operating Account / Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-Low. Samoa has no domestic digital-bank or electronic-money-institution licensing regime, and offshore EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Mercury, Wise Business) legally may service a Samoa IC but routinely decline Pacific offshore entities due to jurisdiction risk and limited compliance appetite. Where an EMI is obtained, the IC must present its SIFA-licensed registered-agent introduction, certified certificate of incorporation, UBO certificate, and source-of-funds dossier through the provider's enterprise program. The resilient structure is anchor bank accounts at ANZ/BSP Samoa paired with a USD-linked EMI wallet used solely for high-frequency, small-ticket app-store fee disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Samoan statute categorically requires physical attendance, but ANZ Samoa and BSP Samoa apply in-person or bank-approved video KYC interviews for IC directors and UBOs as standard underwriting practice. Remote opening is attainable through an exception path: certified identification, notarized board resolution for account opening, video-conference due-diligence interview with at least one signatory director, and a written introduction from a SIFA-licensed registered agent holding an established banking relationship. Fully anonymous or no-interview onboarding is not available; at minimum, a verified-signatory interview and registered-agent attestation of good standing are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from a PRC/HK family trust or a high-risk jurisdiction without a clear wealth-origin trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified trust deed summary or trust instrument excerpt; 12 to 24 months of verified bank statements from the settlor/trustee funding account; independent asset valuation reports; notarized source-of-wealth letter (accumulated income, dividends, M&A liquidity); tax-residency certificate of each UBO; notarized gift or loan agreements; board resolution authorizing the capital call; and a documented family-trust structuring rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt IC flagged as lacking economic substance, commercial nexus, or genuine business purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Engagement letters from a SIFA-licensed registered agent and licensed secretary; director and officer service agreements; SIFA certificate of good standing and tax-exemption status; physical or virtual office lease; EdTech platform architecture narrative; end-user license agreement (EULA); content-licensing contracts; App Store and Google Play developer registrations; bookkeeping sample; and projected revenue forecasts evidencing real commercial flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: App-store subscription revenue (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) generating payment-consolidator red flags and BOP narrative mismatches
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program and Google Play Console registrations naming the IC as legal developer; consolidated monthly settlement reports from Apple/Google; merchant and payment-acquirer agreements; ISIC 6201 scope description and commercial-model memorandum; end-user terms and privacy policy; IRS Form W-8BEN-E (for US withholding reduction on app-store payments); and a treasury transaction-flow diagram tracing each user purchase to payout and final bank credit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid circular movement of funds among the IC, family trusts, and holding companies indicating layering or tax-arbitrage
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart disclosing all UBOs; intercompany treasury, management, and licensing agreements; arm's-length transfer-pricing memorandum; board minutes approving each treasury movement; audited or management financial statements; confirmation of IC exemption from Samoan income tax; and periodic reconciliation packs submitted to the relationship manager on a standing-review basis.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital should be transmitted by SWIFT MT103 from the settlor, trustee, or shareholder account to the IC's USD account at ANZ Samoa or BSP Samoa. The wire narrative and remitter BOP purpose code must map to direct investment, using the narrative 'Subscription of share capital in Samoa International Company' for equity or 'Shareholder loan advanced to Samoa International Company' for debt. The receiving bank requires a pre-agreed onboarding transaction pack: certified certificate of incorporation and constitution; board resolution authorizing the share issue or loan; UBO certificate and source-of-funds declaration; CBS exchange-control declaration (where the bank's compliance requires it) endorsed with the IC's section 77 exemption; executed subscription acknowledgment or loan agreement; and beneficial-ownership register extract. Funds should remain USD-denominated and be credited to the capital escrow or operating account without WST conversion. Apple/Google settlement batches arrive as a separate inbound rail — consolidated payout remittances from global app-store treasury nodes with remittance advices reconciled by the bank against the developer-program contracts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for content licensing, subcontractor engineering, localized marketing, and group management fees clear exclusively through SWIFT-mediated rails: customer credit transfers via MT103 supported by underlying agreements, invoices, and applicable withholding certifications, and interbank MT202 where the beneficiary operates through a correspondent overlay. Commercial documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) are not applicable to pure software-as-a-service licensing but become permissible if the IC expands into hardware-enabled language-device sales requiring collateralized settlement. Samoan statutory payables — registered-agent fees, SIFA registry fees, licensed director fees — are discharged in WST through the licensed bank's EFTPOS/VDS channel or the CBS RTGS system, funded by a minimal USD-to-WST conversion. The account bank will require a standing transaction-justification framework identifying each counterparty, underlying agreement, and economic purpose to prevent shell-indicia or circular-flow flags.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/WST FX forwards — available through ANZ Samoa and BSP Samoa as authorized-dealer products, conditional on documentary proof of underlying commercial exposure and CBS exchange-control reporting; speculative outrights are prohibited.

Offshore USD/WST non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — legally accessible in principle through global counterparty banks, but the WST offshore NDF market is exceptionally thin; execution is practical only in small notional sizes through regional desks.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) with a Samoan licensed authorized dealer — permissible in theory for balance-sheet hedging of WST liabilities, but an active onshore swap curve does not exist; given the IC's USD-functional-currency status, actual execution is rarely required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; payment due on the renewal date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a surcharge; continued non-payment beyond six months may result in administrative strike-off, restoration costs, and loss of limited liability protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties may be imposed; persistent failure to file can trigger deregistration after formal notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit applies to Samoa International Companies. A statutory audit may be required only by order of the Registrar, by the company's constituent instrument, by shareholder resolution, or by the law of a foreign parent group for consolidated reporting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies are not prescribed local GAAP; books may be kept under IFRS, US GAAP, or another internationally recognized standard, provided that records enable a true and fair presentation of the financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a beneficial ownership register at its registered office in Samoa and confirm annually, together with the annual return, that the registered shareholder and beneficial ownership information is accurate. Any share transfer during the year must be recorded in the register and reflected in the sworn confirmation signed by the registered agent or director.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Samoa International Company (IC) is statutorily exempt from corporate income tax under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); effective CIT rate is 0% on all foreign-source and non-Samoa income. No capital gains tax applies in Samoa. The IC is ring-fenced and may not derive Samoa-source income; the only recurring public charge is the annual Government fee (approximately WST 1,000–2,000, depending on authorized capital). General resident corporations are taxed at 27% with no broadly applicable preferential rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SAM-IC-AR (Annual Return of an International Company), filed via the Samoa International Companies Registry electronic portal administered by the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); International Companies do not file corporate income tax returns because they are tax-exempt — the Annual Return and annual Government fee constitute the sole recurring compliance filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual filing is due within 30 days following the anniversary date of incorporation; the annual Government fee must be settled on or before the anniversary date. No statutory extension of time is available; grace periods are granted only at the Registrar's discretion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the International Company and its registration number, exactly as recorded on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registered legal name; trade names and foreign business identifiers are not accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date of incorporation and jurisdiction of incorporation, which must read Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the registry record; any discrepancy must be corrected through the registered agent before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa maintained by the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign street addresses cannot be substituted; the registered agent's Samoa office must be stated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and licence number of the Samoa-licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select a corporate service provider licensed by the Samoa authorities; the agent is jointly responsible for the accuracy of this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized share capital, currency (WST or USD), and class of shares, which determine the tier of the annual Government fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the authorized capital in the currency adopted at incorporation; under-declaration triggers penalty reassessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued share capital, number of issued shares, and the form of consideration paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State whether the EdTech subscription business shares were issued for cash, IP consideration, or services; non-cash consideration must be described.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors' full names, nationalities, and residential addresses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident and nominee directors are permitted; at least one director's identity must be provided for customer due diligence, and CDD files must remain with the registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Beneficial ownership declaration under Samoa's AML/CFT framework, which is non-public.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Lodge the beneficial ownership schedule directly with the licensed agent; it is not part of the public register and is disclosed to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit only upon lawful request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of compliance with the International Companies Act, confirming that no business has been conducted within Samoa and no Samoa-source income has been derived.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IC ring-fence must be strictly confirmed; breaching this declaration converts the exemption into taxable residency at 27%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Digital revenue nexus attestation (best practice): confirmation of the payment rails (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) and the absence of any physical, employee, or server nexus in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the group structure and revenue flow so that foreign tax authorities can verify economic substance outside Samoa; this mitigates CFC recharacterization risk.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Annual Return attracts a penalty of WST 100 per month or part-month, plus a 10% per annum surcharge on the unpaid Government fee; persistent default leads to strike-off and dissolution of the company, with contracts entered into during the struck-off period rendered void.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by a Samoa International Company under the statutory exemption in the International Companies Act 1987; the general non-resident dividend withholding tax rate under the Income Tax Act 2002 is 15% and would apply only if the company were taxable in Samoa.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For Samoa IC dividends no withholding arises at source and no treaty relief is required. Where a taxable dividend, interest, or royalty is paid and treaty relief is sought under Samoa's principal DTAs with Australia and New Zealand, the non-resident payee must: (i) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority; (ii) submit the TRC together with the Samoa reduced-withholding application (WHT-R form) to the Samoa Revenue Corporation before the payment distribution date; and (iii) retain underlying ownership documentation proving beneficial entitlement to the income. Relief is implemented either as reduced withholding at source or as a refund mechanism.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents under the Income Tax Act 2002 is 15% for each category; under the Samoa-Australia and Samoa-New Zealand DTAs, interest is typically limited to 10% and royalties to 5-10%, depending on the industrial, commercial, or copyright character of the payment; software subscription and intellectual-property licensing royalties must be characterized carefully to determine the applicable treaty rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa prescribes no explicit statutory threshold in Samoa Tala (WST) for Local File or Master File preparation; as best-practice compliance for this EdTech subscription business, contemporaneous OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation (Local File, Master File, and a benchmark study) is recommended whenever aggregate annual controlled transactions exceed WST 500,000, or whenever high-margin IP-embedded subscription revenue is repatriated to a connected party outside Samoa.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa applies the statutory ring-fence doctrine under the International Companies Act 1987 rather than a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) filing regime: the IC must maintain a registered office and licensed agent in Samoa but is prohibited from carrying on any domestic business or deriving Samoa-source income. For this Apple IAP / Google Play Billing subscription business, no Samoa economic substance is required; however, the beneficial owner's home tax jurisdiction may apply CFC or economic-substance standards, so the IC should retain board minutes, IP development records, and revenue allocation models evidencing genuine management and activity outside Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of subscription revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing in the beneficial owner's residence-country tax return while the Samoa IC files no return anywhere; synthetic allocation of digital profits to a tax-exempt IC lacking any substance, personnel, or function.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2002, the Samoa Revenue Corporation may raise default assessments for understated income, impose penalties up to 200% of the tax evaded, add incremental late-payment surcharges, and prosecute officers; conviction carries a fine and imprisonment of up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false compliance declarations face criminal prosecution, civil restitution orders, travel bans issued by the Supreme Court of Samoa, asset freezing, mandatory attendance for examination, and disqualification from holding directorships; the corporate veil is pierced where the IC is used as a sham to defeat tax claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming or maintaining the Samoa IC without any licensed registered agent, registered office, board governance, or accounting records, and channeling EdTech subscription receipts through the shell with no discernible business purpose other than tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may strike off and dissolve the company, charge monthly default penalties (WST 100 per month plus 10% per annum on overdue fees), vest residual assets in the Registrar pending creditor claims, refuse restoration, and render contracts concluded during the struck-off period void.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors incur strict personal liability for all debts incurred while the company is struck off; creditors and tax authorities may proceed directly against personal assets; a court may order restitution and impose a travel ban pending settlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa IC and digital payment rails to launder proceeds, failing to maintain beneficial-ownership records, refusing to cooperate with the licensed agent's customer due diligence, or failing to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit once suspicion has arisen.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and supporting AML/CFT regulations: fines up to WST 1,000,000 for corporate entities, confiscation and freezing of tainted proceeds on FIU application, and up to 10 years' imprisonment for individuals convicted of money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally prosecuted for willful blindness; personal freeze and forfeiture orders may be made against their assets, and the court may impose personal travel restrictions and disqualification from financial-services roles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized Domestic Business / Breach of IC Ring-Fence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting Samoa domestic operations, including hiring Samoan-based tutoring staff, establishing a local content studio, or deriving Samoa-sourced subscription income, while holding International Company status in breach of the statutory ring-fence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IC loses its exemption: the Income Tax Act 2002 applies retroactively at the 27% corporate rate, with interest on unpaid tax, late-filing penalties, and default-assessed taxes on all Samoa-source revenue; the Registrar may also strike off the company for breach of the International Companies Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved local business are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax; enforcement may include personal bank levies, asset freezing, travel bans, and criminal fines, overriding limited-liability protection.
